clue.text: Notice to prepare domicile

parts.note: an ad is a notice, short for advertisement
to dress food or a wound is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get their home ready for visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: A domicile is where someone lives, and an address names that place of residence.

clue.text: Envoy failed to complete certificate

indicators.note: not completing a word means its final letter never arrives

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent abroad

explanation.surface: An ambassador did not finish the course and so got no qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: DIPLOMAT loses its last letter to leave DIPLOMA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diploma is a document awarded on completing a course of study, a kind of certificate.

clue.text: Beginners to read about small southeastern civet

indicators.note: the beginners of the following words are their opening letters only

parts.note: opening letters of these three words
SE is the compass abbreviation for southeastern

explanation.surface: Novices are told to look up a small civet from the southeast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small' looks like part of the definition but supplies only its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The rasse is a small Asian civet, a cat-like mammal of southern China and Southeast Asia.

clue.text: Foolish parson gains nothing in giving voice

indicators.note: something foolish is muddled, so the letters are jumbled into new order

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A silly clergyman gains nothing by singing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gains' simply adds O to the parson's letters before they are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest singing voice, and the word names the voice type itself.

clue.text: Animal barrier at rocky bay

parts.note: a wall is a barrier

indicators.note: rocky suggests something unsteady and shaken up, so the letters move

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fence stands by a rocky inlet to keep animals in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' reads as describing the bay's shore, but it scrambles the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A wallaby is an Australian marsupial, a smaller relative of the kangaroo, so an animal.

clue.text: One battle site away from home

parts.note: a means one
a field of battle is where fighting happens

explanation.surface: A single battleground lies far from where the soldiers live.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means at a distance, especially away from one's usual place, as in 'far afield'.

clue.text: Restrict Mr Dennis — son remains unrestricted

parts.note: to restrict is to limit
Les Dennis is a British TV presenter and comedian
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: An instruction to rein in a TV host, while his son stays free.
explanation.walkthrough: Les Dennis presented the British game show Family Fortunes.
explanation.definitionFit: Limitless means without any bound, the same as having no restriction placed on it.

clue.text: Good French red drunk by you first when parched

parts.note: bon is French for good

indicators.note: a drunk is unsteady, so the letters stagger into new places

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fine French red, drunk by you before anyone else when thirsty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like drinking the wine, but it jumbles the word red.
explanation.definitionFit: Bone-dry means completely without moisture, an intensified way of saying parched.

clue.text: Doctor animating spry insect

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A medic livens up a nimble bug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a noun, a physician, but it works as the verb meaning tamper with.
explanation.definitionFit: The praying mantis is a predatory insect named for the way it holds its forelegs together.

clue.text: Post Office retrospective of American work

indicators.note: retrospective means looking back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: PO is the abbreviation for Post Office
US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A postal exhibition looks back on an American's work.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic composition, a creative work, as in magnum opus.

clue.text: Westminster average: I delve into complaint

parts.note: par is the standard or average level

indicators.note: to delve into is to dig inside, so one letter goes inside another word

parts.note: a lament is an expression of grief or complaint
taken as written

explanation.surface: An ordinary politician digs into a grievance at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Westminster' looks like a place, but here it stands for the institution that sits there; par is golf's standard score.
explanation.definitionFit: Westminster is used as a metonym for the British Parliament, which sits in the Palace of Westminster.

clue.text: Drink store's plastic badge with ring

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are remoulded

parts.note: taken as written
a ring is shaped like O

explanation.surface: An off-licence's cheap plastic badge comes with a ring attached.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodega is a Spanish wine shop or cellar, so a store selling drink.

clue.text: They say you'll have time for this holiday

indicators.note: what people say is heard, so a word is taken by its sound

parts.note: the contraction is pronounced the same as the old word for Christmas
tide is an old word for time or season, as in eventide

explanation.surface: People promise you will get time off for this festive break.
explanation.definitionFit: Yuletide is the Christmas season, the main winter holiday period.

clue.text: Lover loses right to acquire books that are most important

indicators.note: losing something means a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: a paramour is an illicit lover
R is the abbreviation for right
NT is the New Testament, the books of the later Bible

explanation.surface: A jilted lover gains books that matter most to them.
explanation.walkthrough: PARAMOUR drops its final R and then adds NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Paramount means supreme, above all others in rank or importance.

clue.text: A trapper first promises to snare fabulous bird? That's abominable!

indicators.note: a snare traps something inside it, so one part goes within another

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: opening letter of the word
the roc is a giant bird from Arabian legend
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A hunter vows to catch a mythical bird, which is outrageous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from fable here, not wonderful; the roc carried Sinbad in the Arabian Nights.
explanation.definitionFit: Atrocious means appallingly bad, a close synonym of abominable.

clue.text: Woman of stone

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a female first name
second meaning: a gemstone, of which emerald and aquamarine are varieties

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a hard-hearted woman; it is a girl's name that is also a precious mineral.
explanation.definitionFit: Beryl is both a woman's name and a mineral prized as a gem, so a precious stone.

clue.text: Ward off with prayer at right time

parts.note: an Ave is a Hail Mary prayer
R is the abbreviation for right
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Keep evil away by praying at the proper moment.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a danger is to prevent it or turn it aside, the sense of fending it off.

clue.text: Plant carried in beer van

indicators.note: things that are carried get moved about, so these letters shift position

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A potted plant is transported in a brewery's delivery lorry.
explanation.definitionFit: Verbena is a flowering garden plant, also called vervain.

clue.text: Read man's first paper, put straight and sign

indicators.note: to put something straight is to sort out a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word after it

parts.note: opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Instructions to read a man's first document, tidy it, and sign it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's first' looks like the selection, but the first letter taken is the one from paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampersand is the & sign, a symbol standing for the word and.

clue.text: Five deleted from otherwise relevant constant

indicators.note: otherwise means in a different way, so the letters take a different order
something deleted is struck out, so a letter is removed

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone edits a document, cutting five items that would otherwise be pertinent.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing V from RELEVANT leaves seven letters that are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means unchanging and everlasting, so constant in the sense of never ending.

clue.text: Ran up to traitor at one point to tell tales

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a rat is someone who betrays or deserts
E, East, is one point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone hurried to a betrayer at one stage to inform on others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tell tales' sounds like snitching, but here it simply means to recount stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrate is to recount a story, so to tell tales in the literal sense.

clue.text: Tear up two articles about dangerous fish

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word reads backwards

parts.note: to rip is to tear
the indefinite articles an and a

explanation.surface: Someone shreds a couple of newspaper pieces on predatory fish.
explanation.walkthrough: PIRANA is an older spelling of piranha. 'About' links the pieces in the sense of 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: The piranha is a South American freshwater fish with razor teeth, notorious for being dangerous.

clue.text: King in fiction creates discord

indicators.note: in places one element inside another word

parts.note: taken as written
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A monarch written into a novel stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Friction is conflict or disagreement between people, the same as discord.

clue.text: Half of them cough when they board

indicators.note: half of a word means only part of its letters survive

parts.note: taken as written
a bark is a harsh cough

explanation.surface: Passengers half of whom splutter as they get on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half of THEM is kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to go aboard a ship or aircraft, so to board it.

clue.text: Runner, for example, getting round to party

parts.note: a runner bean is a type of bean
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An athlete makes a lap before heading to a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' wants to be an athlete; it is the runner bean, a common British climbing bean. Beano is British slang for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A beano is an informal British word for a noisy celebration or party.

clue.text: Cleverly coordinate the trimming

indicators.note: done cleverly suggests skilful rearranging of the letters

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to match the edging neatly on a dress.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimming is ornamental edging added to clothes or a cake, a kind of decoration.

clue.text: One route abroad

parts.note: a means one
a way is a route

explanation.surface: A single road leads to foreign parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Being away means absent from home, which is the sense of being abroad.

clue.text: Pussyfoot or creep

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally a cat's foot, read whimsically
second meaning: a toady used by another for their own ends

explanation.walkthrough: Pussyfoot and creep both suggest moving stealthily, but one is read literally and the other means a fawning dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat's-paw is a person used as a tool by another, like the cat in the fable who pulled chestnuts from the fire.

clue.text: Let everyone find love and marry!

parts.note: all means everyone
love is zero in tennis, written O
to wed is to marry

explanation.surface: A cheerful call for everybody to fall in love and get married.
explanation.definitionFit: Let, as a past participle, means permitted, which is what allowed means.
